messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] lkj_cov_log isn't compiling (through generated cpp code).
parts:
I see what the problem is (see below) and
can fix it tomorrow.

On 9/8/12 11:06 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> I don't have it in me right now to check why it doesn't work, but it's
> having trouble with the template instantiations.

There are a couple of problems with how those
are implemented.

First, they're using matrix ops when you can't
guarantee homogeneity of type. For example,
line 73 of lkj_corr.hpp multiples arguments
of type of eta (template param T_shape) and type
of L (T_covar).

lkj_cov.hpp, line 62 and the dup code on line 142
declare D to be a matrix of type double instead
of template type T_y. So if the sampled variate (of
type T_y) is a parameter (stan::agrad::var), it
doesn't look like it'd compile.

> I don't have a unit test in there now showing where it doesn't work,
> but most of the matrix distribution functions don't have accompanying
> agrad tests.

We should add those at least insofar
as we can with finite diffs.

> For the time being, I'm pulling it out of the function signatures and
> the manual. The other lkj_co* functions do compile.

Hopefully we can put them back in when
the functions are working again.

- Bob
